how.en: A text says you have an outstanding traffic contravention or fine and gives a link to pay it. The link leads to a fake website made to look like the agency’s, which takes your card details. LESA has said these messages are not from it.

text.en: A text from “LESA” says you have an unpaid traffic fine.
It warns the fine will go up or go to court if you don’t act soon.
A link takes you to a page to pay the fine by card.
Your card details go to the scammers.
LESA: An outstanding contravention is registered on your vehicle. Settle €35.00 by tomorrow to avoid additional charges and a court summons: [link]

en: contravention on my car by SMS
A fine you can only pay through a link in a text.
Threats that the fine will rise or go to court within a day.
A website you reached from a text rather than by typing the address yourself.
Don’t open the link. Check any fines on LESA’s official website by typing its address yourself.
If you paid or entered card details, call your bank at once.
Report the text to the Police Cyber Crime Unit.

sources.title: MTCA warns public over fake tax refund websites
